PullRequest.Title: Editor window: Explorer title, Worktrees submenu in the folder location picker, close buttons for the chat area and the empty editor area
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## What

Editor window polish from feedback: the chat area (`chat.viewSessions.openInChatPart`) closes chats like an editor group and hands chats over as the setting changes; the empty editor area gets a close button; the folder location UI is simpler.

## Changes

- **Explorer:** title drops the location.
- **Folder Location** (`folderLocationStatusBar.ts`): the entry also shows at the folder's own location with worktrees. The picker groups locations under their provider's label (optional `IWorkspaceFolderLocationProvider.label`, `getLocationGroups`; the agent host supplies "Worktrees"), with the folder last. It opens with nothing expanded; only the current location is checked and announced. Left leaves a submenu; Escape closes the picker.
- **Chat area close:** in Single mode the title shows Close (X). Closing a chat shows the previous one, then a New Chat, then hides the area; with tabs, the last tab hides it. Close All, last in a header's More Actions in both modes, closes every chat and hides the area. The list is restored lazily, most recent first (`agentsChatPart.ts`).
- **New Chat in Single:** one unsent composer is reused, aimed at the full requested target. Typed text is kept (on close, Close All, or when a newer draft takes it), stored across reloads, and returns with the next composer.
- **Hide Editor Area:** an X on the empty group while the chat area shows (`layoutActions.ts`).
- **Runtime toggle** (`chatViewOpenInChatPart.contribution.ts`): turning the setting on or off moves the shown session, or an unsent draft with its input, to the other host. A Local chat closes from the Chat view while local chats are hidden.
- **Seam:** additive `IChatViewHostService.requests`.

## Notes for reviewers

- A draft doesn't move after a newer request or a change to its source.
- Windows tests cover folder comparisons (drive, UNC, case).
- New Chat keeps reusing the unsent composer; a kept draft returns once that composer is sent or closed.
- The Command Palette picker stays a flat list.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` agentsChatPart, agentsChatPartActions, chatViewOpenInChatPart, chatWindowComposer, folderLocationStatusBar, contextkeys: all passing, 0 failing (new tests failed first)
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob` over the chat host, agent host, sessions, workspaces and workspace services tests: 684 passing, 0 failing
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/**/*.test.js"`: 2019 passing, 0 failing
- Live in Code OSS: close order, Hide Editor Area, runtime toggle

## Merge order

Merge main in once #348852 lands.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed filter leaves previous completed chats in the group. ViewEditorPane.hideOrDisposeView explicitly caches every view whose input remains in that group, without eviction; ChatView.setVisible(false) only hides its widget and does not release its registered _modelRef. The retention chain is explicit; its measured byte cost depends on transcript sizes.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Hidden ChatEditorView/ChatWidget trees, detached DOM, and strongly held IChatModelReference transcript models
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N distinct completed chats visited and not explicitly closed in one group, retains N full views/models, with transcript memory proportional to the sum of their sizes, instead of one current completed-chat view/model. Restored inactive entries are initially lightweight; full retention grows as entries are displayed.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Growing retained heap and GC pressure during ordinary conversation browsing
Findings.PreviousBehavior: In Single mode, opening another completed chat closed the previous chat's editor, disposing its cached ChatEditorView and releasing its ChatView model reference. At most the current completed chat, plus deliberately preserved composers, remained.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every previously visited completed chat now remains an open, pinned editor so that Close can return to it. This also keeps its entire rendered chat view and loaded transcript alive, not just its history entry.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The former _replaceOthers closed every other editor except non-pristine composers. The added condition `!!this._chats.get(editor)?.isComposer` in _closeUntouchedComposers now excludes all completed-chat inputs from cleanup, and _open opens every chat pinned.
Findings.Title: Release inactive chat views while keeping Single-mode history
Findings.Impact: With the default Single mode, browsing many distinct, long agent conversations accumulates full hidden widgets, transcript models, and detached DOM until those chats are explicitly closed or the window ends, causing growing memory and GC pressure despite displaying only one chat.
Findings.Evidence: AgentsChatPartService._open opens pinned editors and then calls the changed cleanup. src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/viewEditorPane.ts:193-207 keeps a hidden view in hiddenViews whenever group.contains(input), and removes it only when its input closes. ChatEditorView owns ChatEditorContent/ChatGroupView and their ChatView. src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/browser/chat/chatView.ts:1160 stores the acquired transcript in _modelRef; setVisible at 1561-1568 only changes visibility. The editor limit is disabled by default (workbench.contribution.ts:475-478).
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the history entries and saved view state, but dispose inactive Single-mode view/model instances or use a small bounded cache; recreate evicted views when Close returns to their history entry.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse and close conversations in the default Single-mode chat area
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the requested chat must create or reveal its editor and bind its transcript. Previous conversations are now left open; closing the current one reveals its predecessor. Memory retention continues off the opening critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hydrate session and exact-chat subscriptions and convert backend turns into chat history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold content resolution per distinct displayed chat; session subscription shared for chats of the same session, exact-chat subscription per chat. Same-resource concurrent loads are coalesced by ChatService and ChatSessionsService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cold-load boundary existed. Single mode closed the previous completed-chat input and disposed its view; the diff instead extends full view/model lifetime across navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold conversation display waits for history hydration; existing loaded models avoid it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N distinct completed conversations displayed without explicit close, and the sum of their transcript sizes; repeated visits to the same entry do not add another view.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Ordinary browsing opens chats sequentially. Same-key model loads coalesce; the reported issue is accumulation over time, not an assumed N-way load burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ViewEditorPane.hiddenViews retains the full view while its input remains in the group. ChatView keeps its model reference when hidden. There is no view-cache eviction, and the editor-count limit is disabled by default.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the changed cleanup predicate through group membership, hiddenViews ownership, and ChatView._modelRef; confirmed hiding does not release the model.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No heap measurements; actual retained bytes and GC impact depend on conversation lengths and how many conversations users browse.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one introduced memory regression: prior completed-chat views were disposed; now N hidden widgets/transcripts remain live alongside the visible chat.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore the chat area after window reload
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Restore parses saved entries, restores composers, registers editor inputs, bulk-opens them inactive, then activates the saved chat. The active transcript must bind before it is usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse saved chat URIs and kept drafts and register restored editor entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(N) saved entries plus draft payload bytes, once per chat-part restoration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All saved entries were already parsed and added, but Single mode discarded inactive completed-chat entries before opening editors. They are now retained as history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs during restoration when the layout restores the chat area visible; hidden chat areas do not restore tabs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the active conversation's content through the existing chat-loading path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Inactive completed-chat entries do not create their views or load transcripts. Only the displayed conversation reaches that load path; restored composers use their existing restore behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The active conversation used the same content-loading path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Active content may load after editor creation; there is no newly introduced eager load of every saved transcript.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Saved conversation count N and restored composer/draft payloads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Composer restoration is awaited in the entry loop; editors are opened through one openEditors call and a final active open. No per-history-item backend hydration was inferred.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Restoration is guarded by _restored/_part. Stored data is read from the workspace storage service. Inactive conversation views remain lazy; ChatModelHold only acquires existing models and has a timeout.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for lazy inactive-view behavior and the restore call flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No startup timing measurements or observed saved-history distribution.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate startup finding. Retaining history entries is intentional; the full-model retention finding applies as those entries are displayed.

Scenarios.Scenario: New Chat reuse, retargeting, Close All, and draft persistence
Scenarios.CriticalPath: New Chat locates an existing unsent composer, optionally retargets it, and opens it. A newly created composer binds a draft model. Closing snapshots sendable input; storage serialization runs on onWillSaveState rather than on every keystroke.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reseed a changed composer target and acquire or load its draft chat model through existing session services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one unsent composer is reused in ordinary Single-mode operation; identical requested targets return without a retarget event. Actual target changes can reseed one draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Explicit New Chat could create another composer and slot; the diff preferentially reuses the existing unsent composer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Draft/model readiness gates composer interaction; no new per-history-item work is added.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Export kept draft attachments and marshal chat identifiers and draft contents into workspace storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized chat-part value per save-state event, proportional to kept-draft bytes and open-entry count, not one storage write per attachment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The chat-part value stored chat identifiers and active index only; live composer inputs already had separate persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous serialization occurs at save-state time; parked inputs are loaded lazily and consumed by later composers.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Open group/editor count, number of deliberately parked drafts, and their text/attachment bytes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Close All starts one closeEditors operation per group with Promise.all; each group follows existing editor-close behavior. Retargeted draft creation cancels superseded creation; model loading coalesces by resource.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Kept inputs are loaded once into _kept and popped when a composer is created; switching to Multiple clears them. Existing composer/model and same-target checks avoid redundant creation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for changed ownership, save frequency, and reuse; no unsupported per-attachment boundary fan-out assumed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large attachment/draft byte sizes are possible but there is no established new hot-path serialization or redundant accumulation trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional high-confidence regression: serialization is save-time, draft retention preserves user-authored data, and composer reuse bounds ordinary unsent-composer creation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle chat.viewSessions.openInChatPart or configured orientation while a session or draft is shown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The asynchronous handover waits for the destination host registration, opens one shown session or one new composer, then copies input/attachments if needed. The configuration change itself does not await the entire handover.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the single displayed conversation in the destination host through existing session loading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero if the destination already shows that resource; otherwise one destination open per toggle, not one per retained chat. Loaded model references and in-flight resolutions are reused by resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Changing the setting did not automatically transfer the shown conversation to the other host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The destination chat waits for its existing load path; only after successful handoff is the source chat-part entry closed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy the current draft's attachment array and transfer its input into the destination widget.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(A) attachment references for one draft; not serialization of all chat history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Drafts stayed in their previous host during setting changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Performed only during an actual runtime handover, after the new composer is available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Runtime toggle frequency and attachments in the single shown draft; unrelated chat-history count does not multiply handover calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A later configuration move cancels the previous handover token; request generations prevent superseded draft writes. Existing service/model loads coalesce by session resource rather than duplicating per caller.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing shown-resource comparison avoids reopening the same destination chat. New Chat reuses Single mode's unsent composer. Startup and availability changes do not initiate handovers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for one-session cardinality, startup exclusion, and coalescing behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold provider latency varies, but the inspected path does not fan out across saved conversations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression: new work is bounded to the requested runtime transfer. Retained inactive conversations are covered by the reported lifetime issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show the folder-location status entry at the primary location and refresh it when providers or worktrees change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial alternate lookup is scheduled for window idle. Status display can update after provider results; editor startup does not await the lookup. Later relevant events initiate refreshes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize the local agent-host session-summary inventory with listSessions when it has not been listed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One host-wide list per cold provider store, coalesced while in flight; successful inventories remain valid and are updated by notifications. Empty successful results are cached too. Failures can retry on later asks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The status contribution did not ask for alternates at primary location. Other existing folder-choice/API consumers could already have initialized the same provider cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the editor-startup critical path; provideLocations returns currently known summaries without awaiting listing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the current workspace folder's real path for matching backend project identities.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached/coalesced realpath per workspace-folder identity, with retries after failure and retirement when folders leave the workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This read occurred when another existing location consumer first asked; the status contribution can now be that first consumer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Lookup starts asynchronously; currently known forms are returned immediately and changes are announced later.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One eligible local single-folder workspace, P registered location providers, S cached session summaries, and distinct offered worktrees W.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: getLocationGroups invokes providers with Promise.all. The local provider has one in-flight inventory refresh and cached realpath promises. Workspace-folder and can-set-location events can both refresh, but these share the provider's expensive work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The status contribution remembers whether any alternates exist. Actual expensive reads are cached/coalesced in the provider and list store; warm refreshes compute from summaries. Provider change notifications are based on offered-location differences, not every streaming token.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the actual provider instead of treating the status contribution's Git comment as proof of subprocess work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session-inventory size and provider initialization cost are unmeasured; no new per-session subprocess or IPC fan-out was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the newly requested discovery is bounded and cached, does not directly run Git in this implementation, and is off startup's blocking path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the grouped folder-location picker and select a worktree or primary folder
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The picker appears immediately with seed entries, then fills from provider groups. Selection awaits existing location resolution, trust handling, and the queued workspace/configuration switch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask providers for alternate locations and, on selection, resolve the chosen location against the local agent-host inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One enumeration call per registered provider per picker opening; no calls per submenu item. The local provider reuses its inventory and realpath caches; resolution can await one coalesced refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: getLocations already queried every provider with Promise.all. Grouping changes result shape and menu construction, not provider-call cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Enumeration does not block initial picker display; selected-location resolution gates the switch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve destination identity/trust and initialize configuration for the selected folder through the existing workspace switch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected-folder switch, not one switch per listed worktree; returning to the current folder short-circuits configuration replacement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The flat picker already called setFolderLocation once for the selected URI with the same trust/configuration path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The selected switch awaits trust/configuration work; workspace mutations are serialized through workspaceEditingQueue with freshness checks.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P providers and W deduplicated location entries; submenu action creation is O(W), comparable to previous flat row creation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider enumeration is parallel; selected-location provider resolution is sequential until resolved; actual workspace mutation is queued. No per-row backend operations are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Grouping uses the same provider caches. Picker lifetime owns a cancellation token; resolved results are ignored once cancelled. A concurrent status lookup shares the local provider's costly initialization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged backend call structure and serialized switch ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large menus may have UI costs, but no concrete diff-introduced scaling regression beyond similar O(W) construction was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: richer grouping and submenu metadata do not change expensive boundary count or move full discovery onto initial picker presentation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hide the empty editor area and render the simplified Explorer title
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new close action invokes the existing setEditorHiddenByChat layout transition once. Explorer name retrieval uses the same workspace label helper without the location option.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Explicit close-action invocations and existing title refresh frequency, not chat-history or worktree count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI action and existing layout machinery; no new loop, repeated geometry read, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network call was found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache ownership, invalidation, or retained collection is introduced by these hunks.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the bounded changed action and label call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Existing layout duration is unmeasured, but the diff introduces no repeated/scaling layout mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 21 changed files and all paginated diffs, with targeted caller/lifecycle/cache and boundary tracing. Submitted one high-confidence medium-severity finding for full hidden chat view/transcript retention in Single mode. Other changed scenarios did not establish separate actionable performance regressions. Static read-only review; no performance measurements were invented.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
